header:
Date: 2026-10-21 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Martinez (CISO - Crestfield), Daniel Reeves (CTO - Crestfield), Maya Singh (Compliance Lead - Crestfield)
summary: Discovery focused on data residency and compliance requirements for Crestfield Financial. Customer prioritizes EU data residency (GDPR), strict logging restrictions for PII/HIPAA-like data, and SOC2/ISO evidence. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options, VPC/on-prem tradeoffs, KMS/HSM, RBAC, and audit logs. Agreed next steps: send security pack, performance spreadsheet, and schedule legal/infra deep-dive.
topics: Data residency: EU-only requirements and cross-border controls
Logging restrictions: redact/no logs for sensitive PII and regulated transactions
Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
Security certifications: SOC2, ISO, penetration testing
Encryption & key management: KMS, HSM, customer-managed keys
Operational controls: RBAC, audit logs, retention policies
Performance: latency vs cost tradeoffs for Dedicated vs Hosted
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Avery from Redwood, i'll kick us off. Samir's our solutions engineer as well.
[00:08] Laura Martinez: Hi, thanks. we're Laura, CISO at Crestfield. We have Daniel (cto) and Maya (compliance) here. We're trying to understand how Redwood can meet our data residency and logging constraints for financial workloads.
[00:20] Samir Patel: Great, thanks. quick agenda — understand your regulatory needs, discuss options (hosted/dedicated/private), and outline next steps. sound good?
[00:28] Daniel Reeves: Yep. high level: we're building a conversational assistant for retail banking customers and some backend inference for document processing. must be GDPR compliant for EU customers and there are also bank-specific rules about logs and audit trails.
[00:40] Maya Singh: Also, certain transaction data is sensitive — we can't have raw transcripts persisted beyond 24 hours, and logs that contain account numbers need to be redacted or never leave our environment.
[00:52] Avery Chen: Understood. can i ask where your current stack runs and how you handle keys / encryption?
[01:00] Laura Martinez: We're primarily in AWS eu-west-1. keys are in our KMS account. some of our POCs used managed apis but we kept everything in house for sensitive flows.
[01:10] Samir Patel: ok. so when you say "logs can't leave our environment," do you mean no plaintext request/response stored on Redwood side, or you need the ability to opt out of logging entirely?
[01:20] Maya Singh: Ideally opt-out for certain flows. For others we can allow metadata-only logs with request IDs, latency, but no content. and anything that is stored has to be encrypted with our keys.
[01:33] Daniel Reeves: We also need to know about subprocessor locations — are backups replicated to US regions? cross-border replication is a no-go for EU resident accounts.
[01:43] Avery Chen: For Hosted, our default is multi-region for HA, but we have EU-only tenancy and we offer Dedicated and Private where data plane stays in customer VPC or on-prem. we can provide EU-only hosting and avoid cross-border replication for that tenant. there are tradeoffs on latency and cost.
[01:59] Laura Martinez: So Hosted EU-only — are logs ever processed in a US control plane? do you have access to keys?
[02:07] Samir Patel: Good Q. Our control plane communicates with the data plane for orchestration; we can provide a private control plane option for Private deployments. For Hosted EU-only, metadata and metrics can be aggregated to our control plane, but we can limit the payloads — we also support customer-managed keys in some Dedicated/Private plans so Redwood doesn't have raw key access.
[02:28] Maya Singh: Customer-managed keys is important. If we upload encryption keys to HSM in our cloud, can Redwood use them for disk-level encryption only, or for application-level encryption of logs too?
[02:38] Samir Patel: With Dedicated/Private + customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key), you can enforce that logs at rest are encrypted with your KMS. application-layer encryption of payloads is possible via tokenization / client-side encryption, but that adds latency and complexity.
[02:54] Daniel Reeves: Latency is sensitive — we target p95 < 300ms for interactive prompts. what's typical for Hosted vs Dedicated?
[03:02] Samir Patel: Typical Hosted p95 varies by model and seq length; for small gen models we see 150–350ms for short prompts but for longer context tokens can be higher. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower variance — for your 200 rps pattern (is that about right?), we can architect GPU pools with KV cache pinned to reduce cold starts.
[03:22] Laura Martinez: Yes around 150–250 rps during peak. Also concerned about logging retention policies — regulators ask for retention of audit logs for 7 years sometimes, but we can't keep content-level logs that long.
[03:34] Avery Chen: We support per-route retention policies and can redact request/response bodies before storing. for high-compliance customers we recommend Dedicated + VPC or Private so you control storage retention.
[03:46] Maya Singh: Do you support redaction rules that run before any payload leaves our network? ie, we want to strip account numbers client-side and only send masked text.
[03:56] Samir Patel: You can implement client-side masking — Redwood can also provide SDK hooks and middleware to redact on the edge before reaching our servers. for Private deployments you can keep that entire flow inside your VPC.
[04:10] Daniel Reeves: How about auditability — we need immutable audit trails for who called what model and when. but that trail cannot include PII.
[04:18] Avery Chen: We have RBAC, request-id tracing, and audit logs. logs can be configured to store metadata only (user id hash, route, model version, timestamps) and redact content. for Private, we can stream audit logs to your SIEM.
[04:30] Laura Martinez: Certifications — do you have SOC2, ISO 27001, pen test reports? HIPAA attestation?
[04:36] Samir Patel: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we have ISO 27001 scope; we also have penetration test summaries. HIPAA is handled per-customer in Private/Dedicated contracts — we can support HIPAA-compliant setups but require a BAA and Private or Dedicated with customer controls.
[04:56] Maya Singh: Okay so for EU customers we need GDPR data subject rights — ability to delete or export data. if we host EU-only, can end-user data be purged on request?
[05:06] Avery Chen: Yes, we support data deletion workflows and can run subject access request exports for records within retention windows. with Private deployment you have direct control.
[05:15] Daniel Reeves: There's also a procurement question: if we go Hosted EU-only, what's the SLA and what about backups that might be geo-redundant?
[05:24] Samir Patel: Hosted has standard SLA tiers; Dedicated offers stronger SLA with reserved capacity. Backups for EU-only tenancy are kept within EU footprint; we can provide details in the security pack.
[05:33] Laura Martinez: On logging restrictions: if we annotate that certain endpoints are "no-log", will that be enforced across your stack including compute proxies and observability agents?
[05:44] Samir Patel: For Dedicated/Private, yes — you can set no-log routes at the edge and those payloads are never persisted. For Hosted, we have no-log flags we can honor, but some operational telemetry (metrics) may still flow to our control plane as aggregated numbers.
[05:58] Maya Singh: What's the uplift and cost difference between Hosted EU-only and Dedicated? high level numbers would help.
[06:06] Avery Chen: Broadly, Dedicated is higher monthly committed cost but lower per-token and more predictable latency. Hosted is pay-as-you-go with slightly higher per-unit price but faster time-to-market. i'll send a cost comparison with an example workload.
[06:20] Daniel Reeves: For our security team we need to see network diagrams and where control-plane components live.
[06:26] Avery Chen: We'll include network diagrams in the security packet. we can also set up a private control plane for Private deployments to address that.
[06:33] Laura Martinez: Can you clarify how key rotation works if we bring our own key? and do you support HSM-backed keys?
[06:40] Samir Patel: Yes, we integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can also support customer HSMs via dedicated connectors for Private. key rotation can be driven by your KMS policies; Redwood can re-encrypt storage with rotated keys as part of a maintenance window.
[06:55] Maya Singh: We may need to limit where logs are searchable — only in our SIEM. can you stream audit logs to an S3 bucket in our account?
[07:03] Avery Chen: Absolutely. for Dedicated/Private we can stream logs to your S3 or SIEM via secure forwarding. Hosted can also forward logs if you opt in, but for highly restricted flows we'd recommend Private so nothing leaves your VPC.
[07:18] Daniel Reeves: Any gotchas with GDPR and subprocessors? we need a list of subprocessors and subcontracts.
[07:25] Samir Patel: We'll provide a subprocessors list and DPA. Hosted customers get the default list; Dedicated/Private gives you more control and narrower subprocessors since infrastructure can be customer-managed.
[07:37] Laura Martinez: Ok, let's talk about PII detection and automatic redaction. Do you provide built-in redaction or do we need to build it into our pre-processing?
[07:46] Samir Patel: We provide some automated PII detection heuristics and SDK middleware; however, for bank-grade compliance you should have pre-processing client-side tokenization to guarantee no sensitive fields are sent. we can help with patterns and examples.
[08:00] Maya Singh: For legal we'll want to review the DPA and BAA. who signs those?
[08:06] Avery Chen: Redwood legal will sign DPA and BAA for enterprise customers; we'll route those via your procurement.
[08:12] Daniel Reeves: Great. any performance constraints if we do application level encryption before sending?
[08:18] Samir Patel: yep, client-side encryption will increase payload sizes and CPU on the client, and we won't be able to do model-side caching effectively unless we implement a cache key strategy. it will increase latency — we can model it in the spreadsheet.
[08:32] Laura Martinez: One more — retention: we might need to keep metadata audit logs for 7 years, but content must be purged in 24 hours. can you guarantee content purge?
[08:41] Avery Chen: We can guarantee purge workflows for Dedicated/Private with contractual SLAs. for Hosted we'll commit to operational policies and can demonstrate via logs/attestations but recommend Dedicated for contractual guarantees.
[08:55] Maya Singh: Ok that's helpful. next steps?
[09:00] Avery Chen: Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs, network diagrams, subprocessors list, and a cost/latency comparison. Samir will create the perf spreadsheet for 200 RPS. you (Maya) will send constrained data categories. we'll schedule infra/legal deep-dive for 11/02.
[09:18] Daniel Reeves: sounds good.
[09:20] Laura Martinez: thanks, looking forward to the security pack.
[09:23] Samir Patel: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links to docs and a calendar invite for the deep-dive.
[09:30] [call ends]
